# Patches for `vizsoft-global/DPD-userapp`

Source changes behind the APKs in the parent directory. They could not be
pushed to the driver app repo directly — the Cursor GitHub App is only
installed on `MG-GO-Admin`, so pushing to `DPD-userapp` returns 403.

Both apply cleanly on `main` @ `e726d08` and are independent of each other.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vizsoft-global/DPD-userapp
cd DPD-userapp
git checkout -b remove-splash-screen
git am /path/to/0001-Boot-straight-to-the-login-screen.patch
git am /path/to/0002-Let-ABI-splits-scope-native-libraries.patch
flutter pub get
```

## 0001 — Boot straight to the login screen

Cold start used to sit on the splash for roughly 6.5 seconds. `SplashScreen`
would not navigate until `assets/images/splashvideo.mp4` finished playing —
9.80 seconds of footage at 1.5× playback — and it separately waited on a
driver-app-settings fetch.

`GoRouter`'s `redirect` already resolves session, maintenance mode and blocked
state; the splash route was simply excluded from it by an `if (onSplash)
return null;` early return. Starting at `/login` lets that existing logic run.

- `initialLocation` moves from `/` to `/login`
- the `/` route and the `onSplash` early return are gone
- `lib/features/splash/` is deleted
- `video_player`, `assets/images/splashvideo.mp4` and `assets/images/splash.svg`
  are removed — nothing else referenced them (`flutter_svg` stays, it is still
  used by `branding_logo.dart`)
- `macos/Flutter/GeneratedPluginRegistrant.swift` regenerated by `pub get`

**Behaviour change to be aware of:** maintenance mode is no longer resolved
before the first frame. A driver briefly sees the login screen and is then
redirected to `/maintenance` once the settings fetch resolves, through the
existing `settingsRefreshListenable`. Previously the splash blocked for up to
5 seconds waiting for that answer. If maintenance must never be bypassable for
even a moment, gate the login form's submit button on
`appBrandingProvider.hasValue` rather than reinstating the splash.

`flutter analyze` reports the same 39 pre-existing issues before and after, all
of them in `test/` (those files import `package:dpd_userapp/...` while the
package is named `mg_go`) plus four warnings in `lib/`. This change adds none.

## 0002 — Let ABI splits scope native libraries

`flutter build apk --split-per-abi` fails on `main`:

```
Conflicting configuration : 'arm64-v8a' in ndk abiFilters cannot be present
when splits abi filters are set : armeabi-v7a,x86_64,arm64-v8a
```

The `ndk.abiFilters` block was not achieving its stated intent anyway — the fat
APK still shipped `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a` and `x86_64`, and the arm64 build
declared all three in its manifest while carrying the Flutter engine for only
one. On an emulator or a 32-bit device that installs and then crashes at launch
on a missing `libflutter.so`.

Removing the block lets `--split-per-abi` emit one correctly-scoped APK per
architecture, each declaring exactly the ABI it ships.

## Unfixed: the splash video played audio out loud

Worth knowing even though patch 0001 makes it moot by deleting the video. The
asset carried a real AAC track — mean volume −29.7 dB, peaking at −6.7 dB — and
`splash_screen.dart` never called `setVolume(0)`, so every cold launch made
noise through the speaker. If the intro is ever reinstated, mute it.
